freezing-of-gait-video.title: Freezing of Gait (Video)
freezing-of-gait-video.html:
Please watch these videos and keep an eye on the clients feet. Shuffling or freezing of gait an happen when walking is initiated or mid walk when the client stops. Freezing can also happen when there is a change in floor surface or a going through a doorway.


This is one client's first class with us and after one session he had improved his freezing with proper cueing. Having the client FEEL the changes you are showing them is key to them implementing these changes at home and not just in the gym.

start-up-equipment.html:
Getting Started: Your Path to Launch

Setting up your Boxing 4 Health program is a step-by-step process, and this checklist walks you through it from start to finish. You'll begin by securing a teaching location and diving into your online training, then move into hands-on practice with current clients while you learn. From there, you'll plan your pilot program, source your boxing bags and equipment, and build out your referral contact list — including the neurologist outreach that's one of B4H's strongest tools for filling classes. Finally, you'll pull together your marketing assets to spread the word. Work through each section in order, check off tasks as you go, and don't hesitate to reach out to Christine (christine@boxing4health.com) for program questions or Tina Cousineau, PT (tina@boxing4health.com) for clinical questions along the way.

class-breakdown-overview.title: Class Breakdown Overview
class-breakdown-overview.html:
Our classes are broken down into the following- here


Warm up- 7-10min

High Intensity- Mix between functional exercises and Boxing technique and drills. 32-35min

Cool down- Gentle stretching and or ball work(using self massage balls) 10-15min


We have 3 types of classifications for our fighters.

Fighter

Champion

Champion Plus


**Once your assessment with the client is complete you will then be able to place the student in the appropriate class.


Our Fighter Classes- are higher intensity and are set up as circuit based classes.


-These classes are best for those that have low to moderate balance concerns. -Exercises are Parkinson’s specific and include amplitude-based movements and dual tasking. -Cognitive exercises will also be added in these classes.


Our Champion Classes- are lower intensity and are set up as a group class vs a circuit class. They are a mix of Champions and Champion Plus clients.

Please read the document below to see the difference between these two clients.

cool-down.html:
Stretching and releasing are very important for the PD population. A 5-10 minute cool down involving stretches, breathing and massage ball work is a perfect way to end the class!

Overall, muscle rigidity is relatively common amongst people with PD. Be mindful of your fighters' limitations when selecting components of your cool down session.

volunteer-orientation.title: Volunteer Orientation
volunteer-orientation.html:
Volunteers

They are there to help you run a safe, fun and high energy class!

Please get them as involved as possible.

Once they are familiar with your gym have them help with setup and take down of equipment.

Holding pads (if they are trained to do so). SAFETY is our first priority so please don’t encourage untrained volunteers to hold pads.

Show them box of cognitive games to go around and use with students during class (flash cards, math cards, etc.)

Having them work one-on-one with a specific student is TOP priority (client having an off day, client with a DBS, higher fall risk/unstable, cognitive slowness).

Challenge them to find ways to get students to use their voice more in class.

Have them run a warm up if they are interested.

IMPORTANT to review volunteer expectations with family members especially with low functioning as you may need them to help when you are low on staff or volunteers.


Where do we get Volunteers from?

Retired Seniors who have an interest in giving back and are relatively healthy depending on what class you need them in.

University / College students: Reach out to university departments that have placement programs (i.e. Kinesiology, Neuroscience, Fitness and Recreation) to see if they need placement opportunities as MOST do!

High school students: Most HS Students need forty (40) hours of volunteer work but make sure to screen them to see how willing and able they are to work with our population and the importance of their commitment.


Our classes are divided into 4 segments. The segments consist of a Warm Up, Functional Exercises, Boxing, and Cool Down. The goals each of segment is the same for both Fighter (High Functioning) and Champion (Low Functioning) classes. The Fighter classes consist of higher functioning participants and allow more freedom with exercise selection. The Champions classes require more careful exercise selection, more modifications and a slower/more consistent pace.


This is the volunteer orientation we send to all of our volunteers and ask that they watch it in full before starting with us. It gives them a basic understanding of the population.

class-tools.html:
We use this app in class and project it to a TV screen. You can also use an IPAD because we find that having a visual for the clients can be beneficial.

We also use HIIT timers when we teach a group functional or boxing portion. So play around with options and see what works best for you!

Free app- Boxing iTimer


MUSIC- we use Spotify you can check out our playlists at Boxing 4 Health. Music plays an important part in a class and it helps motivate the clients, helps with their rhythm and timing as well. Sometimes breaking out into dance during a class is a great way to have some fun and get the clients to loosen up too;)

We also ask clients what they want to listen to and make playlists based on that too. Typically its a mix rock classics of 60's, 70's and 80's.

Health History & Liability Forms: Examples to Get You Started

Every B4H program needs a Health History form and a Liability Waiver in place before your first class. These are essential for participant safety and your own protection as an instructor. Included here are the forms we use at Boxing 4 Health HQ, provided as examples you're welcome to use as-is or adapt to fit your specific location and setup. If you already have your own health history or liability forms through your facility, your professional regulatory body, or your own practice, feel free to use those instead. The important thing is that some version of both is in place before you open registration.
